svg.title: A confirmed order changes the safe return decision
svg.desc: Four fictional local states in reading order. Before cutover, both stores contain the same orders. After target-only order e is confirmed, a guarded return refuses the old source and a forced return makes the order disappear from the visitor's view. Only after checked reverse replay and reconciliation can a guarded local return find the order. The illustration does not test DNS, independent writers, external effects, or cloud cutover.
svg.text: A confirmed order changes the return.
A route is safe only if the customer can still find accepted work.
1 Before cutover: compare both stores
Old and new contain orders a, b, d.
The target now serves visitors.
GET d → 200 from target
2 Target accepts a new order
Visitor submits e for 250 cents.
The old store still has no e.
POST e → 201 confirmed
3 A backward route now loses the order
Guarded return refuses the old store.
A forced old route hides confirmed e.
GET e → 404 from old
4 Replay and check before returning
Copy e back; reject conflicts.
Compare stores, then select the old route.
GET e → 200 from old
Local SQLite and loopback route only.
No writer fence, DNS, CDC, external effects, or AWS cutover.
